meta.title: A 7-slide consulting deck: market entry strategy for a new OEM entering the India electric two-wheeler market. Slide plan: 1) title slide, 2) executiv

slides.title: India’s electric two-wheeler market offers a credible entry window for a new OEM with a focused segment-first strategy
slides.subtitle: Market entry strategy for a new OEM in India electric two-wheelers

slides.title: India’s electric two-wheeler market is attractive for entry if the OEM targets commuter scale first, differentiates on trust and distribution, and funds an 18-month launch

sections.heading: Market
sections.body: Large, fast-growing market with demand concentrated in commuter scooters at **illustrative 60%** of volume; premium remains influential for brand pull, while B2B fleet supports early utilization and data learning.

sections.heading: Competition
sections.body: The field is active but still fragmented across Ola Electric, TVS iQube, Ather, Bajaj Chetak, and Hero Vida; incumbents bring reach and trust, while EV natives lead on software, speed, and EV-first positioning.

sections.heading: Entry thesis
sections.body: Enter with a commuter-led portfolio, build credibility through quality and service, use selective premium variants for brand lift, and add fleet partnerships to accelerate volumes, utilization, and product feedback loops.

sections.heading: Ask
sections.body: Approve an **illustrative 18-month** entry program covering product localization, dealer and service build-out, charging and ecosystem partnerships, and a phased launch with clear KPI gates before national scale-up.

slides.title: India’s e-two-wheeler market is attractive, but winning requires segment focus and a clear right-to-win
slides.subtitle: Market attractiveness, segment structure, and entry pockets for a new OEM; illustrative data

slides.title: The commuter segment offers the best beachhead with the largest scale, solid growth, and a price point accessible to a new OEM
slides.subtitle: Illustrative comparison of India electric two-wheeler segments across size, growth, price point, positioning, and leading players

cells.text: Best entry wedge for scale: high-volume urban and semi-urban riders prioritize affordability, range adequacy, and low running cost.
Differentiated but narrower pool: buyers value performance, design, software, and brand; stronger product expectations raise entry risk.
Attractive for contracted demand and utilization, but economics depend on fleet partnerships, service uptime, and financing capability.

summary_band.label: Best beachhead
segments: Accessible **₹90k–₹120k** pricing aligns with mass adoption
Competition is real, but scale and value positioning favor a focused launch

slides.title: EV natives lead growth while legacy OEMs retain scale, leaving whitespace between premium retail and fleet-focused value play
slides.subtitle: Illustrative benchmark of four competitor groups across revenue, units, market share, and growth in the India electric two-wheeler market

insights.text: **Legacy OEMs** combine meaningful scale with slower growth than **EV natives**, indicating incumbents are defending share rather than defining the category.
**Ola Electric** sets the pace on both **₹6,500 crore** revenue and **55%** growth, but concentration among a few leaders leaves room for a differentiated entrant.
**Fleet players** remain small at **1%–3%** share but sustain **25%–32%** growth, suggesting an adjacent entry wedge below mainstream consumer retail.

slides.title: Phased India entry can build a **₹500 Cr** business at **15%** share in the target niche while limiting early-market risk

icon_stats.text: Illustrative revenue potential by Year 5 in the target niche under a phased entry model.
Illustrative annual volume at scale, anchored on focused launch economics rather than all-segment entry.
Illustrative target niche share, concentrated in the most attractive entry segment before broader expansion.
Phased market entry timeline from launch preparation to scale-up, with gates to manage execution risk.

cards.title: Phase 1 launch
cards.body: Enter **1** priority segment with **3** launch cities to validate product-market fit and channel economics.

cards.title: Phase 2 expansion
cards.body: Expand to **10** cities after milestone gates are met on demand, service readiness, and partner performance.

cards.title: Portfolio focus
cards.body: Lead with **1** core platform, then add **2** adjacencies after initial scale and brand proof points.

cards.title: Capital discipline
cards.body: Use **18 months** of phased milestones to sequence investment and reduce exposure versus a national Day 1 rollout.

highlight.title: Recommendation: pursue a phased India entry starting with **1** attractive niche, prove economics in **3** cities, and scale selectively over **18 months**
highlight.body: Prioritize a focused beachhead over broad national entry: build share in the target niche, use milestone gates before city expansion, and preserve flexibility for later moves into **2** adjacent segments.

slides.title: An **18-month** phased plan can validate demand, build channel capability, and launch at controlled scale with limited risk
slides.subtitle: Five sequenced workstreams move from market test to scaled launch while preserving flexibility

bullets.text: **Months 0–3:** Confirm target segment, refine value proposition, and test willingness to pay in **3** priority cities
**Months 3–6:** Finalize product-market fit, homologation plan, and pilot economics; lock initial supplier and service-partner shortlist
**Months 6–9:** Build channel capability through **10** pilot dealers, technician training, and digital lead-generation setup
**Months 9–12:** Launch controlled commercial pilot with **1,000** units, tight KPI tracking, and rapid product/service iteration
**Months 12–18:** Scale into **25** cities with expanded channel coverage, working-capital controls, and go/no-go review for broader rollout
